//: RETIRED_SPELLINGS of the Drizzle alignment of col.* (contract: drizzle-alignment.md). Swept on 2026-11-13 and deleted: an old spelling no longer compiles (the ones a JavaScript caller can still write throw the instruction). tooling/scripts/drizzle-sweep.mts converts a project still written in them. Printers (codemod, schema introspect, the Studio schema editor) already write `new`. `new` builds the identical ColumnDef (packages/common/test/schema/drizzle-alignment.test.ts).
imports: A file that uses `sql` or `pgEnum` imports them from the same entry as `col`: `import { defineTable, col, pgEnum, sql } from "@rebasepro/server/schema"`.

RETIRED_SPELLINGS.note: The SQL name is the builder's leading argument. On an array it goes on the item builder: col.array(col.text()).column("x") → col.text("x").array(). On a pgEnum column: postStatus("x").
After the sweep a bare col.varchar() is refused (unbounded in Drizzle).
After the sweep a bare col.char() is refused (char(1) in Drizzle).
Also col.varchar(n).oneOf([...]) → col.varchar({ length: n, enum: [...] }) and char. .oneOf() stays on number columns and JSON fields.
Same for col.json<T>(). col.jsonb(json.object({...})) is unchanged.
Item modifiers (.validate, .oneOf / { enum }, .userId, .transform, .describe) stay before .array(); column modifiers go after it.
Declare once per module (or in a shared module and import it). col.enum([...]) without a name is unchanged.
col.custom<T>("type") → col.custom({ dataType: "type" }).$type<T>(). After the sweep a lone string is the SQL column name.

UNCHANGED: col.uuid() col.text() col.smallint() col.integer() col.serial() col.smallserial() col.real() col.doublePrecision() col.boolean() col.date() col.time() col.bytea() col.jsonb() col.json() col.geopoint() col.storage({...}) col.enum([...])
